decision: KEEP TypeScript with native byte/stream primitives and explicit runtime admission; FIX missing session byte-boundary regression evidence. No production defect demonstrated in this review.
constraints: Node SDK receiving untrusted API-v1 bytes, with web-standard streams and a P12 consumer; no native mobile deployment or hardware control in this component.

Fixed 65536-byte session accumulation, strict UTF-8, exact profile binding, duplicate/depth rejection and generated schema validation before returning a handle. Cancel/release the reader and avoid transport-detail disclosure on failure.
TypeScript declarations cannot authorize inputs. Keep all admission in executable code. No normalization, changed frozen limits, network fallback or extra deployment runtime.
This bounded transport adapter has no measured native throughput bottleneck or identified hard-real-time host requirement; no language-performance ranking is claimed.

alternatives.technology: TypeScript plus standard TextDecoder/ReadableStream and AJV standalone validation
alternatives.assessment: Selected: direct typed host API use with JavaScript runtime semantics; static declarations add no runtime safety. Explicit fatal decoding, bounded accumulation, lexical checks and schema checks are observable in the executed corpus. No conversion of the host stream into a second runtime heap is required.

Same host execution and mandatory security checks; no demonstrated runtime benefit. TypeScript additionally checks SessionHandle and stream contracts during package compilation and emits the public declarations. Plain JavaScript remains appropriate for the focused test/mutation driver.

alternatives.technology: ReScript compiled JavaScript with JSON/host bindings
alternatives.assessment: Credible typed JavaScript-domain alternative beyond this component language. Its official JSON binding example explicitly does not guarantee input shape; custom lexical and byte/stream admission would still be required. No demonstrated removal of a boundary or correctness defect compared with the tested TypeScript implementation; migration is not justified by type syntax alone.

Credible memory-safe parser option. web-sys imports browser APIs through bindings, so host stream and cancellation boundaries remain. A module artifact and host-memory interface would need parity validation; no measured parsing bottleneck or native shared-core requirement establishes a material win for this small bounded adapter. Reassess if those constraints change.

limits: Nine new tests pass on the baseline: this is missing independent negative coverage, not a newly fixed production failure. Two copied-module mutations produce six expected failures; sources and dist are not modified by the mutation runner.
The complete SSE-event cap versus producer payload-only cap remains an explicitly rejected interoperability fixture and a producing-lane handoff. No silent bound relaxation.
The 65536-byte accumulator is not a total network/heap bound or deadline. Host fetch and stream allocation, never-ending responses and scheduler delays are not qualified by these tests.
No alternative compiler benchmark, browser/device/Windows validation, complete lane audit, P19 acceptance, cryptographic/MLS certification, availability or tactical-deployment claim.
